title: Leica GS18 T Tilt-Compensated GNSS Smart Antenna
summary:
The GS18 T is a multi-frequency GNSS rover with tilt compensation, so the pole never has to be levelled. Push the tip to the point, tip the pole, and the instrument compensates for the tilt up to 30 degrees while you keep working.

The tilt solution uses no magnetometer, which matters on real jobsites: it stays accurate in steel, on machinery, and around vehicles, where magnetometer-based instruments drift. For a crew that spends its day setting control, shooting detail, and checking as-builts, that removes the levelling step entirely.

555 channels, 8 mm + 1 ppm RTK on a single baseline, 4G LTE and an optional UHF radio for base-to-rover work over the site.
specs: RTK single baseline: H 8 mm + 1 ppm / V 15 mm + 1 ppm; network RTK H 8 mm + 0.5 ppm / V 15 mm + 0.5 ppm
Tilt-compensated RTK: additional H uncertainty under 2 mm + 0.3 mm/degree down to 30 degrees tilt, no magnetometer used
Static and rapid static: H 3 mm + 0.5 ppm / V 5 mm + 0.5 ppm; static long H 3 mm + 0.1 ppm / V 3.5 mm + 0.4 ppm
1.23 kg instrument, 3.53 kg standard RTK rover setup on pole; 173 x 173 x 109 mm
Li-ion 2.8 Ah / 11.1 V, up to 8 h; IP66 / IP68, operating -40 to +65 degrees C
accessories: Leica TS13 robotic total station for a hybrid GNSS and total station setup: the total station tracks a prism on the antenna
UHF radio antenna kit for base-to-rover
Battery charger and spare Li-ion battery
